data.description:
# `parity._recall_false_accept` computes specificity but the gate fails when it RISES

## Problem

`parity._recall_false_accept` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py`) computes the fraction of items gold
says are CLEAN (`label != "block"`) that the runner correctly did NOT block. That is specificity
/ the true-negative rate: HIGHER IS BETTER. But `parity_report` gates it as
`if (fa2 - fa1) > NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN` -> "false-accept rose", so a candidate is FAILED for
false-firing LESS than the baseline. The docstring's stated intent ("false-accept =
wrongly-shipped / safe") describes the opposite quantity: of the items that SHOULD have blocked,
the fraction not blocked (1 - recall).

## Evidence (measured, story 0d76)

The frontier slot of the live Bedrock provider-parity run failed partly on
`false-accept rose 0.143 > margin 0.02`, v1 0.786 -> v2 0.929. The 0.143 is exactly two
gold-ADVISORY cases (2/14) on which direct Anthropic FALSE-FIRED and Bedrock did not. The
candidate was penalised for being more accurate. See
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`.

## Why it matters

This is a gating criterion on rebar's non-inferiority bar. It authorized the LangGraph ->
pydantic-ai cutover and is now being applied to Bedrock (epic 061c). As written it can fail a
strictly better candidate and pass a strictly worse one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide and document which quantity the criterion is meant to be, and make the computation,
      the name, the docstring and the gate direction agree.
- [ ] A test pins the direction: a candidate that false-fires LESS than the baseline must not be
      failed by this criterion; one that ships more should-block items must be.
- [ ] Re-score the recorded provider-parity results against the corrected bar and record whether
      the frontier slot's verdict changes.
data.title: parity false-accept criterion is inverted: it gates specificity as a failure rate
